Order 
With the consent of learned counsel for the parties, the appeal is finally heard.

2. This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been preferred by the appellants/claimants being aggrieved by the award dated 01.08.2022 passed in MACC No.167/2021 by the Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Mandsaur, whereby a total sum of Rs.11,32,000/-
has been awarded to them by way of compensation.

3. As per the appellants, on 29.06.2021, at about 2:00 am Nizamuddin Kazi, husband of appellant No.1, father of appellants No.2, 3 and 4 and son of appellant No.5, was returning from village Bahi NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:11746 2 MA-5453-2022 Parsvanath on his motorcycle.

When he reached near power grid on Mahu- Neemuch Highway, respondent No.1 drove the vehicle bearing registration No. MP 4 ME 0342 which was owned by respondent No.2 and was insured with respondent No.3 in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the same against his motorcycle, as a result of which he fell down and suffered grievous injuries.
He was taken to the hospital for treatment, but eventually expired.
4. The appellants, thereafter, filed an application under Section 166 of the Act, 1988 before the claims tribunal for award of a total sum of Rs.65,65,000/- to them by way of compensation.

1 application was contested by respondent No.3 by filing its written statement to the same.

sentences.text: Upon evaluation of the evidence brought on record by the parties, the Claims Tribunal has awarded compensation to the appellants as aforesaid.

5. This appeal for enhancement of the amount of compensation has been preferred by the appellants on the ground that the income of the deceased which was taken by the tribunal at Rs.6,000/- per month is extremely low.
The deceased was in the business of selling and purchasing old vehicles hence his income ought to have been assessed appropriately.

He was aged about 47 years and was looking after his family hence it could not have been assumed that his income was only Rs.6,000/-
per month.
It is hence submitted that the amount awarded to the appellants be enhanced appropriately.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:11746 3 MA-5453-2022 6.

Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.3/insurance company has submitted that just and fair amount of compensation has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal to the appellants, in which no interference is warranted in view of which the appeal deserves to be dismissed.
7. I have considered the submission of learned counsel for the parties and have perused the record.
8. The deceased was aged about 47 years at the time of his death.
He was having the responsibilities of taking care of his family which included his wife, three children and his mother.
It was categorically stated that he was doing the work of purchasing and selling old vehicles.
In view of the work being done by him it could not have been expected from the appellants to produce any documentary evidence in that regard.

The accident had taken place in the year 2021 and if the income of the deceased is taken on the basis of minimum wages then the same would be Rs.8,400/-
per month.
For loss of dependency, appellants would be entitled for sum of Rs.8,400/- + 25% for future prospects of rise in income i.e. Rs.2100/-, total Rs.10,500/- i.e. Rs.1,26,000/- per annum.
The deduction of 1/4th made and the multiplier of 13 applied by Claims Tribunal is appropriate.
For loss of dependency the appellants would be entitled for a sum of Rs.12,28,500/-.

9. Thus, the appellants are entitled for award of a total sum of Rs.14,83,000/- to them by way of compensation whereas the claims NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:11746 4 MA-5453-2022 tribunal has erred in awarding them a sum of Rs.11,32,000/- only.

The appellants are hence held entitled for enhancement in the amount of compensation in the sum of Rs.3,51,000/-
which shall be paid to them along with the same rate of interest as awarded by the claims tribunal from the date of filing of the claim application till the date of payment.
10.
The appellants have valued this appeal at Rs.3 Lakhs whereas the enhancement in the amount of compensation has been made in the sum of Rs.3,51,000/-.
The appellants would hence be required to pay the requisite Court fees on the additional enhanced amount of Rs.51,000/- which shall be paid by them within a period of two months from today.

In case the Court fees is not paid as Arifa Bee vs Sumit on 2 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161054294/
2 aforesaid, this enhanced amount of 51,000/- shall cease to carry any interest after a period of two months.
